summary: The requested output is one fixed boolean decision; empty JSON containers expose no enumerable entry, while a nonempty container can be rejected immediately on its first property or array index without counting or materializing all keys.

optimality.argument: Any correct implementation must produce one boolean decision, requiring Omega(1) work. The reference returns true when enumeration yields no entry and returns false on the first yielded JSON property, using a fixed amount of state.

replacement_checks.evidence: Producing the required boolean for a supplied container requires at least one constant decision.
The reference stores no key collection and returns on the first enumerable property; an empty object or array enters no loop iteration.
Authored cases cover empty objects and arrays, ordinary properties, array indices, null and falsy values, nested empty containers, and an empty-string key.
